patient.name: Miriam Vanderberg
patient.chief_complaint: Burning pain in feet and hands since age 22, now spreading — multiple physicians have told her 'nothing is wrong'
patient.hpi: Miriam Vanderberg is a 34-year-old graphic designer who has had progressive burning neuropathic pain in her feet since age 22, now involving her hands and lower legs. She has been evaluated by 4 prior physicians including 2 neurologists, all of whom told her standard nerve conduction studies were 'completely normal' and some suggested her symptoms might be anxiety or fibromyalgia. She describes constant burning and aching pain in her feet, worse at night, which prevents her from sleeping. She reports allodynia so severe that bedsheets touching her feet are intolerable. Over the past 3 years, symptoms have extended to her calves and hands. She also reports episodes of episodic facial flushing and sweating disproportionate to ambient temperature, abdominal cramping, constipation alternating with diarrhea, and near-syncope on standing that her internist attributed to dehydration. Her mother had identical symptoms starting in her late 20s and was told she had fibromyalgia before dying at age 59 of 'heart failure of unclear cause.' Her maternal uncle has severe burning foot pain and uses a wheelchair. Her 10-year-old son has intermittent painful episodes in his hands and feet exacerbated by fever. She has no diabetes, no alcohol use, no toxic exposures, and no history of chemotherapy. Multiple metabolic, rheumatological, and infectious workups have been negative at outside institutions. She was diagnosed with 'small fiber neuropathy of unknown etiology' 2 years ago when an outside institution performed skin biopsy, but no further workup was initiated to find the cause. She has trialed gabapentin 1800 mg/day, duloxetine 60 mg, amitriptyline 50 mg, and topical capsaicin with insufficient relief.
pmh: Small fiber neuropathy (diagnosed 2 years ago by outside institution, cause unknown)
Prior diagnoses considered: fibromyalgia, anxiety disorder, functional disorder (all incorrect)
patient.review_of_systems: Positive: burning neuropathic pain feet and hands (since age 22), progressive allodynia, nocturnal pain worse, episodic facial flushing and sweating, orthostatic near-syncope, GI dysmotility (constipation + diarrhea + cramping), heat intolerance, anhidrosis patches on feet and legs (absent sweating). Negative: muscle weakness, joint swelling, rash, dysphagia, diplopia, bowel/bladder incontinence, cognitive impairment.

family_history: Mother: burning foot pain from age 28, fibromyalgia label, died at 59 of unexplained cardiac failure. Maternal uncle: severe burning foot pain, wheelchair-bound. Son (age 10): episodic painful crises in hands and feet triggered by fever and exercise. Father: healthy, no neuropathy. AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT INHERITANCE PATTERN — mother, index patient, and son affected across 3 generations.

social_history.note: Graphic designer working from home. Married. Non-smoker. Non-drinker. No illicit drugs. No toxic occupational exposures. Severely limited quality of life from pain — stopped exercise 3 years ago.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x4. Normal cognition. Visibly distressed due to pain.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No facial sensory loss (cranial nerve small fiber involvement not tested by standard exam).
neurological_exam.motor: STRENGTH FULLY PRESERVED. 5/5 throughout all muscle groups. No wasting, no fasciculations.
neurological_exam.sensory: SMALL FIBER MODALITIES SELECTIVELY IMPAIRED. Pinprick: reduced bilateral feet to mid-calf (stocking distribution). Temperature: unable to detect warm/cold at feet bilaterally (tested with metal objects). Vibration: NORMAL at medial malleoli and toes. Proprioception: NORMAL at toes. Light touch: normal at feet (preserved large fiber A-beta mediated). Upper extremities: mild pinprick reduction bilateral hands — glove distribution.
neurological_exam.reflexes: FULLY INTACT. Achilles 2+ bilateral. Patellar 2+ bilateral. Biceps 2+ bilateral. Triceps 2+ bilateral. Diffusely normal reflexes — preserved large fiber myelin (contrast to large fiber polyneuropathy).
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact. Finger-nose and heel-shin normal. No ataxia.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal gait. Normal tandem walking. Negative Romberg (proprioception intact — large fibers normal).
neurological_exam.special_tests: Allodynia: severe bilateral feet — light stroking with cotton gauze provokes burning pain (C-fiber sensitization). No muscle tenderness. No palpably enlarged nerves. No pes cavus. Normal reflexes with pain out of proportion = SFN pattern.

findings.test: Skin biopsy IENFD (3-mm punch, distal leg)
findings.result: 1.4 fibers/mm (reference: 8.1 ± 3.4 fibers/mm at age 34; 3.3 SD below normal)
findings.interpretation: Severely reduced IENFD — confirms small fiber neuropathy with objective anatomical evidence

findings.test: QSART (quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test, bilateral feet and legs)
findings.result: Bilateral feet: 0.00 uL (absent sweating). Bilateral lower legs: 0.04 uL (severely reduced; reference >0.6 uL).
findings.interpretation: Anhidrosis bilateral feet and severe reduction bilateral legs — autonomic C-fiber loss confirmed

output.impression: 1. Skin punch biopsy (distal leg): intraepidermal nerve fiber density 1.4 fibers/mm — severely reduced at 3.3 SD below age-matched normative data. Findings are consistent with small fiber neuropathy. 2. QSART: bilateral feet anhidrosis (0.00 uL); bilateral lower legs severely reduced (0.04 uL; reference >0.6 uL). Sudomotor dysfunction confirmed in a length-dependent distribution. Clinical correlation recommended.

Hereditary SFN Workup.value: No pathogenic variant — Fabry disease EXCLUDED

output.interpretation: Abnormal: SCN9A (Nav1.7) c.2215A>G, p.Ile739Val — pathogenic gain-of-function variant identified. Alpha-galactosidase A enzyme activity, plasma lyso-Gb3, and GLA sequencing: all within normal limits, no GLA pathogenic variant detected. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings: LV size and systolic function normal. EF 58%. No LV wall thickness increase; IVS 10 mm, PW 9 mm, LVM/BSA 78 g/m² (all normal). Valves: mitral, aortic, tricuspid, and pulmonic structurally normal; no significant regurgitation. Pericardium normal. RV normal size and function. Grade I diastolic dysfunction, age-appropriate. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation.
output.impression: Normal transthoracic echocardiogram. LVEF 58%. No wall motion abnormality. No hypertrophy. No pericardial effusion. Consider cardiac MRI for further evaluation if clinically indicated.

output.query: SCN9A Nav1.7 gain-of-function hereditary small fiber neuropathy treatment sodium channel

results.citation: Faber CG et al. (2012) J Neurol.
results.summary: Nav1.7 p.Ile739Val causes constitutive channel activation, DRG neuron hyperexcitability, episodic pain in 3 family members. Temperature sensitivity explains fever-triggered episodes.

Lacosamide (slow sodium channel inactivator) reduces Nav1.7 gain-of-function and provides superior pain relief vs standard treatments in SCN9A-positive patients. Carbamazepine and mexiletine used with variable success. Standard gabapentin/pregabalin less effective for channelopathy-SFN.

output.summary: SCN9A gain-of-function variants (including p.Ile739Val) are associated with hereditary small fiber neuropathy and dysautonomia with autosomal dominant inheritance. Temperature-sensitive channel kinetics underlie fever-triggered pain episodes observed in some family members. Evidence for sodium channel-directed pharmacotherapy (lacosamide, carbamazepine, mexiletine) in SCN9A-positive small fiber neuropathy is derived from case series and small open-label trials. Fabry disease (GLA mutations) is the most common treatable hereditary cause of small fiber neuropathy and should be excluded before attributing disease to sodium channelopathy.

output.proposed: Lacosamide 100-200 mg twice daily + Gabapentin 600 mg TID (current) + Duloxetine 60 mg (current)

interactions.description: Both have CYP2C19 involvement at high doses but no clinically significant interaction at standard doses. Monitor for additive CNS effects.

Carbamazepine is a strong CYP1A2 inducer — reduces duloxetine plasma levels by 30-50%. If carbamazepine used, duloxetine dose adjustment or replacement required. Lacosamide preferred (no enzyme induction).

warnings: QTc monitoring recommended with lacosamide — can prolong QTc slightly; obtain baseline ECG
alternatives: Mexiletine as alternative sodium channel agent if lacosamide ineffective

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hereditary small-fiber neuropathy due to SCN9A (Nav1.7) gain-of-function variant

differential.key_features: X-linked; small-fiber neuropathy with acroparesthesia, angiokeratoma, renal/cardiac involvement; lyso-Gb3 elevated; needs enzymatic + GLA sequencing.
Common autoimmune cause; need anti-SSA/SSB + sicca.
Should not be diagnosed by exclusion alone in the presence of objective IENFD reduction.
Burning extremity pain with erythema and warmth, often SCN9A gain-of-function variants — same gene, overlapping phenotype.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Skin biopsy for intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IENFD below 97.5% lower limit for age/sex confirms small-fiber neuropathy

optimal_actions.action: Autonomic function testing (QSART, deep-breathing HRV, Valsalva)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sudomotor and/or cardiovagal dysfunction supports small-fiber / autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Hereditary small-fiber neuropathy gene panel (SCN9A, SCN10A, SCN11A) and Fabry workup (alpha-galactosidase A activity in males, GLA sequencing in females, plasma globotriaosylsphingosine [lyso-Gb3])
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pathogenic SCN9A variant confirms hereditary sodium channelopathy small-fiber neuropathy; excludes Fabry disease

optimal_actions.action: Sjögren's, paraneoplastic, and autoimmune workup (anti-SSA/SSB, paraneoplastic panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Rule out acquired autoimmune and paraneoplastic causes of small-fiber neuropathy

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize early adult-onset distal burning pain with normal large-fiber findings as small-fiber neuropathy
Skin biopsy for IENFD (diagnostic gold standard)
Hereditary sodium channelopathy panel (SCN9A/10A/11A) given age at onset and family pattern
Symptomatic therapy (sodium channel blockers — mexiletine, oxcarbazepine, carbamazepine) tailored to variant pharmacology
contraindicated_actions: Do not dismiss as functional / fibromyalgia — chronic small-fiber neuropathy is under-recognized
Do not stop at normal EMG/NCS; large-fiber tests cannot diagnose small-fiber neuropathy
key_reasoning_points: Onset in early adulthood + lifelong burning pain + normal EMG/NCS + reduced IENFD = small-fiber neuropathy, likely hereditary
SCN9A gain-of-function variants cause inherited erythromelalgia and small-fiber neuropathy
Fabry disease must be excluded — disease-modifying enzyme replacement / chaperone therapy is available

red_herrings.data_point: Multiple prior physicians told her 'nothing is wrong'
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Three normal EMG/NCS studies do not exclude small-fiber neuropathy; IENFD is the right test.
